name: Bay Area Union Edition — Sheet Metal, Bridge, Port and Marine

stations.why: The shared opener for the shop: a brake, a guard and a hand position are the first sheet metal lesson.
The shop's first machine: a cut list laid out square and sheared with the guards walked, hands behind the finger guard and the drops hooked, never grabbed.
The fitting itself: pressure and seal class off the drawing, a Pittsburgh lock rolled and closed, the flange cornered and the seams sealed to class before the section is stencilled.
The CNC plasma table where the fume control is proven on the manometer before the arc, the zone kept clear through the cut, and the parts hooked off after the cool timer.
A stainless seam run to the shop's procedure under AWS D9.1 with the fume arm on the arc, a fire watch behind the screen and the weld read against the code afterwards.
The run going up on a lift: the anchor's cure card read before any load, trapeze hung and locked, the section levelled and the seismic braces set to the drawing's angle.
The trade's finish work on a boom lift: wind read against the rating, harness on the anchor, panels carried by their returns, clipped, clamped and sealed with nothing loose on the rail.
Testing, adjusting and balancing to ASHRAE 111 and the NEBB procedure: instruments proven, static and flows read at a held fan speed, and the duct walked for the leaks behind the numbers.
A grease duct built to NFPA 96: the joint welded liquid-tight and light-tested, a listed door with listed sealant, clearance measured and the wrap put on layer by layer under a fire watch.
The shared opener for the bridge: connecting steel at height is where every bridge crew starts.
Up a tower leg on a rope grab and across to the platform on a twin-leg lanyard: the permit and rescue plan read, the wind taken, and one leg always on something rated at the transfer.

A cable band from the traveller: the seam and end joints walked for water, the slip read at the witness mark, and the band bolts brought to tension in the charted order, never one slackened out of turn.
A suspender changed under load: the temporary jacks carrying before the old socket is touched, the new rope tensioned to the engineer's figure, pinned, cottered and confirmed.
The lanes closed before the cable is worked: advance sign, arrow board and a taper measured to the plan, set with the traffic and taken down against it, and the traveller run and parked.
Old coatings taken off inside a sealed enclosure: held negative, the strait-side seams smoke-tested before removal, nothing swept dry, and nothing reaching the water.

A blasted patch brought back to International Orange to the specification: the dew point margin taken, the prep and profile checked, edges striped, and the airless pump relieved before its tip is touched.
The foreman's call when the weather turns: everyone aloft down in order of exposure, the deck cleared of what the wind takes first, the traveller brought home and the restart held on the trend.
The deck side of a pier fender repair: a new panel bolted up, test-lifted and lowered over the rail on the tag line to the barge, with the water below held clear.
The shared opener for the port: the lashing deck is where maintenance meets the working terminal.
The spreader on its stands: a below-the-hook device isolated, cycled by hand, measured against its limit and caught lying on its indicator before it goes back on the crane.
The machinery house: the latch proven before the drive is locked, the brake gap a measured number, and the release pressure held under test while the terminal's storm procedure fires.
Stored hydraulic energy as the whole lesson: accumulators bled to zero and proven before a fitting is cracked, the leak found with dye and never a hand.
The reefer row worked to NFPA 70E: the unit down at its own controller before the breaker opens, the plug out dead, and every contact proven live-dead-live.
The wharf edge in a berth window: the vest before the cope, the fender pad measured and slung in, and the bollard's anchors tensioned by the number.
The yard's lighting as its traffic control after dark: the mast tested dead at the handhole, the platform tied off before it moves, and the wind limit read rather than guessed.
The permit's plan as a procedure: the sheen watched, traced upstream and pumped with the outfall gated before the storm's first flush reaches the bay.
A chassis worked chocked or not at all, and its genset isolated before the fuel system opens: the two energies a chassis yard puts in the same bay.
The shared opener for the water: the line under load teaches the snap-back zone before anything else.

The Inlandboatmen's deckhand at the float: the station bill read, the gangway landed before anyone crosses, every passenger counted against the certificate, and the ring buoy to a person in the gap before anything else.
Making up to a barge astern under Subchapter M: the hawser walked and the winch brake set, the eye passed from outside the bight, and the pay-out stopped the moment the wheelhouse goes silent.

The person in charge of a transfer: the declaration signed before the pump, the boom streamed from upcurrent, the flange watched through the slow start, and a sheen stopped at the source rather than dispersed.
The dive station at the surface: the plan briefed, the screw locked out, the standby dressed, the panel never left, and the decompression obligation read from the tables the supervisor holds.
The Pile Drivers' diver under the pier: the umbilical proven by hand, the spall and the section loss found and measured, and every defect photographed against a scale without passing inside a brace.
Under a ship's stern with the shaft and sea suctions locked out: the anodes and coating surveyed, the brush opened only on the plate, and the grating touched only behind its confirmed tag.

Wet cutting and welding to AWS D3.6: the sealed void found, the ground on clean steel before 'make it hot', 'make it cold' before every rod change, and never the diver between the ground and the work.

The standby's dive: the fouled diver reached along his own umbilical, his gas first, the snag cut and never his umbilical, and brought up on the stage at the supervisor's call rather than flown up on a bag.

The small inspection ROV before it ever swims: the thruster shroud bolted on before any call for power, the tether's drag set and its route flown wide of a rebar cage and a ghost net, and the vehicle recalled and docked without ever flying blind on a frozen picture.

A submerged crossing walked cradle to cradle: the locator's gain set before the route is swum, cathodic protection read on the reference cell, and a coating holiday and an undermined cradle found and supported without ever passing under the span or fanning its scour pocket.

A corroded pile jacketed and poured: the form closed and sealed before the tremie ever goes in, its tip kept buried through a pump surge, the air bled at every stage, and the scour bags interlocked once the pour is confirmed full.

The plant's own lockout worked above water first — breaker racked, locked and tagged, the isolation valve shut — before the diver ever proves the no-flow gauge again with their own hands and clears the screen.

A pier's footing read against last year's survey: the benchmark found and the probe zeroed to it before any depth counts, the whole perimeter circled evenly, and the deepest point marked, flagged and logged rather than guessed at.

A dropped skid too heavy for one bag: both shackle pins moused before either bag goes on, the load brought level on the turnbuckle, and the whole rise escorted by eye rather than by a hand ever laid on the load itself.

summary: One Bay Area tool for four union families: the sheet metal shop and the duct run, the Golden Gate Bridge tower, cable and paint programme, the terminal's cranes, fenders and reefer power, and the water itself: ferries, mooring, oil transfer, and the dive stage down to the piles and the hull.
union: SMART sheet metal workers, the Ironworkers and IUPAT bridge crews with the Pile Drivers of the Carpenters, ILWU longshore and maintenance workers with the PMA training programme and IUOE crane maintenance, and the marine unions: the Inlandboatmen's Union of the ILWU, MEBA and SIU, with the Pile Drivers' commercial divers for the underwater work
